sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from $114.5 billion in FY2016 to $184.4 billion in FY2025, a later recast against the $189.0 billion first reported [F1][F10][F177][X10].
The path was cyclical: revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 [D153][D192][D232].
The FY2022 surge came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins, which lifted pre-tax income by $28.0 billion, and net income reached $35.5 billion [P57][F17].
Since FY2022, revenue has fallen at a 7.9% annual rate and net income at 29.8% [D626][D627].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. is the largest driver at 75.1% of FY2025 revenue; its revenue fell 5.3%, subtracting 3.9pp from growth [D402][D403][D404].
US Upstream revenue rose 34.0% to 10.6% of the total, adding 2.5pp, as oil-equivalent production rose 16 percent on the Hess acquisition and Permian growth [D553][D552][D554][P24].
Total revenue fell 4.6% in FY2025 mainly on lower crude oil and refined product prices [D358][P17].
Operating expenses fell 3.4%, less than the 4.6% revenue drop, so revenue growth trailed operating-cost growth by 1.2pp [D373][D358][D379].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% against a 30.5% drop in net income because diluted shares rose 2.1% [D361][D359][D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and the 15.1% high, but above the -5.9% low [F30][D613][D612][D611].
Net margin fell 2.5pp as pre-tax income dropped $7.8 billion on higher upstream depreciation, depletion and amortization, lower realizations and higher operating costs [D369][P9].
Depreciation and amortization rose to 10.7% of revenue from 8.5%, on higher production and higher rates [D341][D299][P12].
Cost of revenue eased to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, while the effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5% [D338][D296][D345][D303].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, and free cash flow of $16.6 billion was 1.35x [F60][D346][F80][D347].
Operating cash flow rose 7.8% as higher TCO distributions and contributions from legacy Hess assets more than offset lower commodity prices [D362][P6].
Free cash flow margin of 8.8% sits just below the 8.9% window median, with capex at 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [D343][D616][D342][D348].
Net cash was $4.0 billion in FY2025 against net debt of $156 million in FY2024, ranking in the 83rd percentile of six energy peers [D351][D309][D637].

That figure uses total debt of $3.3 billion, yet the long-term debt line ends at FY2021 and FY2025 debt issued was $11.4 billion, so net cash and its peer rank likely overstate strength [D350][F166][X157].
Buybacks of $12.1 billion and dividends of $12.8 billion totalled $24.8 billion, or 149.7% of free cash flow [X132][X142][D353][D354].
Diluted shares rose 2.1% in FY2025 despite buybacks, after falling 3.4% in FY2024 [D374][D332].
Revenue declined three years running: 16.5% in FY2023, 1.8% in FY2024 and 4.6% in FY2025 [R1][D274][D316][D358].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 132.8%, 179.7% and 149.7% of it, while cash fell 11.8% in FY2025 [R4][D270][D312][D354][D366].
Data quality: table revenue is a later recast, for example $184.4 billion in FY2025 against $189.0 billion first reported, so growth rates mix two presentations [R3][F10][X10].
Data quality: debt after FY2021 looks incomplete, since total debt falls 84.9% in FY2022 while the filing reports an $8.1 billion decrease [D250][P53].
The cash-burn candidate is benign: it reflects FY2016's negative free cash flow, while FY2025 free cash flow was $16.6 billion [R2][D16][F80].
Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: the gap narrows if FY2026 free cash flow covers the $24.8 billion paid in FY2025, visible in the FY2026 10-K [D353].
Free cash flow margin: it stays below FY2025's 8.8% if capex runs at the guided $18 to $19 billion, versus $17.3 billion in FY2025, per the FY2026 10-K [D343][P4][F70].
Net margin: recovery is confirmed if it rises above the 7.9% window median from 6.7%, as reported in the FY2026 10-K [D613][F30].
